title: Sport: the headless control surface I run my whole Mac from
metaDescription: How I turned a Mac mini into a headless AI workstation I can leave running: one dashboard over every agent, job, service and approval, with a dated progression of how it got there.
dek: A headless control surface for a Mac and a harness over the whole system — every agent, job, service and approval in one shell, with a human gate on anything that leaves the machine.
intro: This started as a card wall of links and turned into the machine's own control surface. One shell now holds the whole system as live state: every agent session and its transcript, every scheduled job and the output it captured, every service and port, every approval waiting on a human, and every deploy. The point is not a pretty dashboard — it is that the Mac does the work unattended and the dashboard exists to report it and to ask for decisions. Anything that leaves the machine, publishing, outbound messages, account changes, stops at an approval gate first, which is what makes leaving it running acceptable.
why: The reason this matters is failure shape. One giant prompt plus one giant tool list fails globally and opaquely. A hierarchy of narrow agents fails locally, in a place you can name, and it can be retried without re-running everything around it. Once you have a durable task bus in the middle, the agents stop being a conversation and start being a system, and a system is something you can actually leave running overnight.

faq.q: Why use several agents instead of one assistant with more tools?
faq.a: Because of blast radius. A generalist with every tool loaded can break anything it touches and its failures are hard to trace. Narrow agents own small surfaces, keep their own context, and can be replaced or retried individually. The hierarchy also means an agent that is good at research never has to hold the credentials for publishing.

faq.q: How do the agents hand work to each other?
faq.a: Through a shared task bus, in this case a SQLite board on the same machine. A card carries the goal, the assignee and its dependencies. Dependencies are modelled as edges, so a card promotes to ready only when its parents are actually done. That is what lets an orchestrator fan work out and fan results back in.

faq.q: What stops an agent from posting or emailing something wrong?
faq.a: An approval gate. Anything with an external side effect, publishing, outbound messages, account changes, stops and waits for a human decision that arrives in a surface I actually read. The gate is not a brake on the automation, it is the reason the automation is acceptable to run unattended.

cta: This one is internal by design, so there is no public link to hand out. If you want this kind of operating layer over your own machine, or you are building one and want to compare notes, the portfolio page is the place to start.
